text:
Defines how StayEase reservations are submitted, confirmed, reviewed and supported. Applies to guest bookings through
approved StayEase channels and internal agents handling booking enquiries.

A confirmed reservation has status “Confirmed” in the authoritative reservation record and an issued confirmation with a
reservation ID. A pending reservation has not reached confirmed status. A rate plan is the price and conditions attached to an
accommodation offer.

• Payment attempt, authorisation, acknowledgement or pending status alone does not prove a reservation is confirmed.
• Agents verify the current reservation record before confirming status to a guest.
• Confirmation details should include property, dates, room type, occupancy, reservation ID, displayed amount, rate plan and
booking-specific conditions.
• Property-specific conditions apply only when displayed before booking and retained in the reservation record.
• Guests should review confirmation details and report discrepancies promptly.

Verify the guest, locate the reservation, compare the confirmation with the current record, classify the issue and follow the
relevant modification SOP. Do not say a change is complete until the authoritative record is updated and any required revised
confirmation is issued.

Follow the approved identity-verification process before disclosing reservation details. For possible duplicate reservations, verify
each reservation ID and route payment/cancellation questions to the relevant policies. Do not promise a refund or cancellation
outcome.

Escalate conflicting status, missing records, property mismatch, duplicate reservations, suspected unauthorised changes,
privacy concerns or conflicting rate conditions.

POL-GST-002 Cancellation & Modification; POL-GST-004 Payment & Billing; SOP-001 Guest Booking Issue Resolution;
KB-004 Reservation Troubleshooting.

Defines the rules for guest cancellation requests and requests to change reservation details. It does not authorise SupportIQ or
an agent to execute a transaction outside approved systems.

Cancellation means ending an existing reservation. Modification means changing dates, occupancy, guest details, room type or
another reservation attribute. A non-refundable rate is a rate whose accepted terms restrict cancellation refunds, subject to
applicable law and approved exceptions.

• Cancellation eligibility, fees and deadlines are determined by the cancellation terms shown to the guest at checkout and stored
with the reservation.
• Agents must inspect the reservation-specific terms; never assume all bookings share one cancellation window.
• A guest request is not a completed cancellation. Completion must be visible in the authoritative reservation record and
confirmed through an approved channel.
• Modification requests are subject to availability, rate differences, property restrictions and any required partner approval.
• Agents must explain any known fee or price difference only when it is explicitly available in the booking record or approved
policy.
• Do not promise a refund amount or processing timeline under this policy; refer to POL-GST-003.

Verify the guest and reservation; retrieve the accepted cancellation terms; establish whether the request is within the applicable
window; explain the recorded outcome; execute only through an authorised workflow; verify the final status; record the
interaction.

Disputes about terms, property-initiated cancellations, system failures, duplicate reservations, medical/emergency claims or
suspected misleading checkout information require the designated escalation path. Do not invent an exception entitlement.

POL-GST-001; POL-GST-003; POL-GST-008; SOP-002 Cancellation Request Handling; SOP-008 Escalation & Incident
Management.

Explains how refund eligibility and refund status are assessed for StayEase guest bookings. Exact outcomes depend on the
reservation, payment record and applicable approved terms.

Refund eligibility is the determination that a payment is refundable under the booking terms or an approved exception. Refund
initiated means an authorised refund instruction has been submitted. Refund completed means the payment provider or source
confirms completion.

• Cancellation does not automatically mean a full refund; determine eligibility from the accepted booking terms and cancellation
outcome.
• Agents must distinguish refund requested, under review, initiated, processing and completed.
• Never state that a refund is complete based only on an internal request or an agent note.
• Any displayed or system-provided estimated timeline must be communicated as an estimate, not a guarantee.
• Do not invent fixed refund timelines, deductions or eligibility exceptions when they are absent from the reservation/payment
record.
• Refunds must return through the approved payment route unless an authorised exception is documented.

Verify guest and reservation; locate the payment transaction; review cancellation/refund eligibility; check whether an authorised
refund instruction exists; communicate the exact recorded status; provide only a sourced estimate; record the case.

Escalate disputed deductions, missing payment references, failed refund instructions, duplicate charges, payment-provider
mismatch, suspected fraud or a refund outside recorded terms.

POL-GST-002 Cancellation & Modification; POL-GST-004 Payment & Billing; SOP-003 Refund Inquiry Handling; SOP-004
Failed & Duplicate Payment Handling; KB-003 Payment Troubleshooting.
Sets support rules for payment status, billing enquiries and payment evidence associated with StayEase reservations.

Authorised means the payment method provider has approved or reserved an amount. Captured means the payment has been
collected. Failed means the provider or platform records an unsuccessful attempt. Duplicate charge means two or more
captured transactions appear to relate to one intended payment.

• Use the payment ledger/provider status as the authoritative source; a bank notification or screenshot is supporting evidence,
not final proof.
• Do not request or store full card numbers, CVV, passwords, OTPs or other authentication secrets.
• Do not equate an authorisation with a captured payment or a confirmed reservation.
• Explain only charges and taxes itemised in the reservation/payment record.
• Never promise a reversal or refund until the authorised workflow and recorded status support it.
• Escalate suspected fraud, duplicate captured transactions, amount mismatch or provider/platform status conflict.

Verify the reservation and transaction reference; identify status and timestamp; compare expected and recorded amount; check
whether the issue is pending, failed, captured or duplicated; follow the relevant payment SOP.

Record the disputed line item and evidence reference. Route tax, invoice or property-collected charge questions to the
responsible billing/property process. Do not make tax or legal determinations.
POL-GST-001; POL-GST-003; SOP-004 Failed & Duplicate Payment Handling; KB-003 Payment Troubleshooting.

Describes baseline guest support rules for arrival and departure. Property-specific hours and requirements must be checked
against the reservation and property record.

• Use the check-in and check-out times shown in the guest's reservation or current property listing; do not assume a universal
time.
• Guests may be asked to present valid identification as required by applicable law and the property's disclosed process.
• Room readiness, access instructions and key collection are property-delivery matters; agents should verify property-specific
instructions before advising.
• An early arrival does not guarantee early room access. Refer early check-in requests to POL-GST-006.
• A late departure is not guaranteed and may incur a property-specific charge only where disclosed and confirmed.
• Do not disclose another guest's room, identity or stay information.

Verify reservation status and dates; confirm the property and guest name; check recorded arrival instructions; contact the
property through approved channels if room access or readiness is disputed; escalate unresolved denial of a confirmed stay.

Confirm the reservation departure date and published property instructions. Route disputed incidental charges or deposit
questions to the applicable billing process.

Escalate a confirmed reservation not recognised by the property, denied access, safety concern, identity mismatch, room not
ready beyond communicated expectations or disputed property charge.

POL-GST-006 Early Check-in & Late Check-out; POL-GST-008 Guest Complaints & Service Recovery; SOP-005 Check-in
Issue Resolution.
Defines how requests for access before the recorded check-in time or departure after the recorded check-out time are assessed.

• Early check-in and late check-out are requests, not guaranteed booking entitlements unless explicitly included in the confirmed
rate plan.
• Availability and approval are determined by the property for the relevant stay date.
• Any additional fee must be confirmed from the property's approved information and communicated before the guest accepts
the option.
• Agents must not guarantee room readiness, access or fee waiver without confirmation recorded through an approved channel.
• If the property cannot accommodate the request, explain the standard time in the reservation and offer only approved
alternatives.

Verify the reservation; identify the requested arrival/departure time; check rate-plan inclusions; submit the request through the
approved property channel; record the property's response; communicate approval, fee (if any) or unavailability.

Escalate conflicting property instructions, accessibility-related concerns, urgent welfare needs or a fee dispute. Do not
independently waive charges.
POL-GST-005; POL-GST-008; SOP-005 Check-in Issue Resolution.
Defines minimum support principles for verifying a guest before disclosing or changing reservation-specific information.

• Complete the approved verification flow before sharing booking details, changing account-linked information or discussing
sensitive reservation data.
• Use only approved verification factors displayed by the support system; do not create ad hoc security questions.
• Never ask for passwords, full payment-card details, CVV or one-time passcodes.
• Do not disclose a reservation to a person merely because they know the guest's name or property.
• If verification fails, limit the response to general policy information and route the guest to the approved account recovery
process.
• Record the verification outcome, not unnecessary identity-document details.

A companion or booker may receive information only where the reservation record or approved authorisation process permits it.
Do not infer permission from relationship claims.
Stop disclosure or changes, preserve relevant case references, and escalate through the security/incident procedure.
POL-GST-001; POL-GST-008; SOP-008 Escalation & Incident Management.

Sets a consistent approach to receiving, recording, assessing and escalating guest complaints about a StayEase booking or
stay.

Listen without blame; acknowledge the reported impact; establish facts; use approved policy; communicate realistic next steps;
protect guest privacy; document actions.

• Property/service quality: cleanliness, room condition, amenities or service not as described.
• Reservation issue: property cannot locate booking, incorrect room or dates, or confirmed booking not honoured.
• Payment issue: unexpected charge, duplicate charge or disputed billing.
• Safety or security: immediate risk, harassment, injury, property access or suspected account compromise.

• Do not admit unverified fault or promise compensation, upgrades, refunds or fee waivers without authorised approval.
• Capture the guest's description, relevant reservation reference, dates, evidence and requested outcome.
• Prioritise immediate safety concerns and route them to the urgent incident process.
• Offer only remedies available in the approved resolution matrix and record who authorised them.
• Keep the guest informed using realistic, non-guaranteed time expectations.

Escalate safety/security incidents immediately through the urgent route; escalate repeated unresolved complaints, significant
service failures, disputed compensation, property refusal to cooperate or potential regulatory/privacy concerns.
POL-GST-003; POL-GST-005; SOP-006 Room Quality Complaint Handling; SOP-008 Escalation & Incident Management.
Defines the baseline onboarding checks for accommodation partners joining the fictional StayEase platform.

• Collect legal business identity and authorised contact details through approved onboarding channels.
• Verify property ownership, management authority or documented right to list the accommodation.
• Collect payout and tax information only through approved secure workflows.
• Review property address, room inventory, amenities, operating status and guest-facing contact details.
• Do not activate a listing until required checks are complete and an authorised reviewer records approval.

Record missing items, assign an owner and request corrections. Activation status must be read from the partner system;
submission of documents alone is not approval.

Escalate inconsistent identity records, suspected document alteration, ownership disputes, sanctions/compliance flags or
requests to bypass mandatory checks.
POL-HTL-002 Listing & Content Guidelines; POL-HTL-006 Account Management; SOP-007 Hotel Partner Support Handling.
Sets quality requirements for partner-submitted property and room content displayed to guests.

• Property name, address, location pin and contact details must be accurate and current.
• Room names, occupancy limits, bed types and included amenities must match the actual offer.
• Images must represent the property and must not materially mislead guests about room type, condition or facilities.
• Descriptions must not claim amenities, accessibility features or services that are unavailable.
• Mandatory fees, restrictions and material conditions must be disclosed in the approved listing fields.
• Content must not include discriminatory, unlawful, misleading or third-party infringing material.

Flag inaccurate or incomplete content; request supporting evidence or correction; publish changes only through the authorised
listing workflow.

Escalate guest-impacting misrepresentation, repeated non-compliance, suspected image misuse or unresolved disputes about
listing accuracy.
POL-HTL-001; POL-HTL-003; SOP-007 Hotel Partner Support Handling.
Defines partner responsibilities and support handling principles for reservations received through StayEase.

• Monitor reservation notifications through the designated partner channel.
• Keep availability, room inventory and restrictions accurate.
• Acknowledge and action reservation requests within the partner portal's displayed service requirements.
• Honour confirmed reservations unless a documented exception and authorised resolution apply.
• Keep guest-impacting changes updated in the partner system and coordinate through approved support channels.

When a partner cannot locate a confirmed reservation, compare reservation ID, property mapping, dates and partner account.
Do not ask the guest to create a second booking as a workaround.

Follow the reservation-specific terms and authorised platform workflow. Partners must not bypass the platform by privately
changing material booking conditions without required guest consent.

Escalate overbooking, confirmed reservation refusal, inventory mismatch, suspected unauthorised changes or repeated
notification failure.
POL-GST-001; POL-HTL-004; SOP-007; SOP-008.
Describes partner-side cancellation controls for reservations booked through StayEase.

• Partners must not cancel a confirmed reservation solely to resell the room at a higher rate.
• Partner-initiated cancellation requires a permitted reason and the approved platform workflow.
• The partner must provide accurate supporting details when requesting cancellation or reporting inability to honour a stay.
• Guest communication and any relocation or recovery option must follow authorised StayEase procedures.
• The guest's refund outcome is governed by the guest reservation terms and POL-GST-003, not by an informal partner promise.

Verify partner identity and reservation; capture the reason and evidence; check booking terms; route for authorised review;
communicate only the approved outcome; record the decision.

Escalate suspected deliberate overbooking, discriminatory refusal, repeated partner cancellations, safety concerns or disputes
about responsibility.
POL-HTL-003; POL-GST-002; POL-GST-003; SOP-008.
Explains the data and control principles for partner commission calculations and settlement enquiries.

• Commission rates and applicable deductions must be taken from the executed partner commercial terms recorded in the
partner system.
• Settlement statements must be reconciled against eligible completed/stayed reservations and recorded adjustments.
• A displayed estimated settlement is not a final remittance confirmation.
• Agents must not invent commission rates, settlement dates, deductions or tax treatment.
• Changes to bank details require the approved secure verification and authorisation workflow.
• Disputed line items must be investigated using statement, reservation and adjustment references.

Verify partner account and requester authority; identify settlement period and statement reference; compare the statement with
eligible reservation records; explain supported line items; raise a finance case for unresolved discrepancies.

Escalate bank-detail changes, suspected payout fraud, missing settlement, unexplained deduction, tax dispute or ledger
mismatch.
POL-HTL-006; SOP-007 Hotel Partner Support Handling.
Defines controls for partner account access, profile changes and authorised contacts.

• Partner users must use individually assigned credentials; shared credentials are not permitted.
• Access must match the user's business role and approved permissions.
• Requests to change legal entity, ownership, payout details or primary contact require additional verification and authorised
review.
• Support agents must not request passwords, OTPs or full banking credentials.
• Deactivation or access restriction must be recorded with reason, authority and effective status.
• Suspected account compromise must be escalated immediately.

Verify requester authority, capture requested change, check required evidence, submit through the approved workflow and
confirm only after the partner record reflects the change.

Escalate ownership disputes, unauthorised access, suspicious payout changes, repeated failed login reports or requests to
bypass verification.
POL-HTL-001; POL-HTL-005; SOP-007; SOP-008.

section: HOW DO I KNOW MY BOOKING IS CONFIRMED?
text: Check for a confirmation message containing a reservation ID and verify that the booking status is Confirmed. A payment notification alone does not prove confirmation.

section: I DID NOT RECEIVE A CONFIRMATION. WHAT SHOULD I DO?
text: Contact support with your reservation ID if available. If you do not have one, support will use the approved verification process to search for the booking.

section: CAN I CHANGE MY DATES OR ROOM?
text: Changes depend on the reservation terms, availability and property approval. Support will check the booking-specific conditions.

section: CAN I CANCEL AND RECEIVE A REFUND?
text: Refund eligibility depends on the cancellation terms attached to your reservation and the recorded cancellation outcome. See the refund status guidance.

section: WHAT SHOULD I DO IF THE PROPERTY CANNOT FIND MY BOOKING?
text: Contact support and provide your reservation ID. Do not create a second booking until support checks the existing reservation and payment status.

section: CAN SOMEONE ELSE CONTACT SUPPORT FOR MY BOOKING?
text: Reservation details are shared only after the approved verification or authorisation process.

section: HOW DO I KNOW ONBOARDING IS COMPLETE?
text: Check the partner portal status or the formal activation notice. Uploading documents does not by itself mean the property is approved or live.

section: HOW DO I CORRECT A PROPERTY LISTING?
text: Submit the correction through the authorised listing workflow and provide accurate supporting details where requested.

section: WHAT IF I CANNOT FIND A RESERVATION?
text: Search by the reservation ID and verify property mapping, dates and partner account. If a confirmed reservation remains missing, contact partner support.

section: CAN I CANCEL A CONFIRMED RESERVATION DIRECTLY?
text: Use the authorised platform process and provide a permitted reason. Do not bypass the platform or make an informal promise about the guest's refund.

section: WHERE CAN I CHECK SETTLEMENT DETAILS?
text: Use the partner settlement statement and reference period. For a discrepancy, contact finance support with the statement and reservation references.

section: HOW DO I CHANGE PAYOUT DETAILS?
text: Use the secure verified account-change workflow. Support will not request passwords, OTPs or full banking credentials.
A pending or authorised payment may not be a completed capture. Check the provider/ledger status and reservation status separately.

section: MONEY APPEARS DEBITED BUT NO BOOKING CONFIRMATION ARRIVED
text: Do not assume the booking is confirmed. Contact support with a transaction reference and approximate timestamp; support will check the reservation and payment records.
Check the provider status and use the approved retry guidance. Avoid repeated attempts until the status of any earlier attempt is understood.
Share the relevant transaction references through the approved secure support channel. Support will determine whether both are captured transactions or one is pending.

section: WHAT DETAILS SHOULD I NEVER SHARE?
text: Never share your password, PIN, OTP, CVV or full payment-card number with support.
Ask support to verify whether a refund was eligible, initiated, processing or completed. Any timeline must be based on the recorded payment-provider estimate.
A pending request is not a confirmed reservation. Wait for the official status update or contact support if it remains unresolved.
Search your registered email/app notifications and contact support with your reservation ID or the details requested for verification.
Provide the reservation ID and stay dates to support. The team will compare the StayEase record with the property mapping.
Contact support. A correction or modification is not complete until the authoritative reservation record is updated.
Do not assume one booking will automatically cancel. Contact support with each reservation reference so both records and related payments can be checked.
Keep the confirmation details and contact support. The team will verify the booked room type and coordinate with the property.
Owns guest reservation, cancellation and check-in enquiries that require specialist review.
Owns payment ledger, refund instruction, duplicate captured transaction and settlement discrepancies.
Owns partner onboarding, listing, partner account and reservation coordination.
Owns suspected account compromise, identity misuse, privacy exposure and safety-related escalation.
Owns serious room-quality complaints and authorised service-recovery review.

Select the issue category and severity in the support system, attach reference IDs and concise evidence, and route to the designated queue. This synthetic directory uses team names only; no personal contact details or live emergency numbers are included.
For immediate danger or medical emergencies, use local emergency services first, then follow the organisation's urgent incident process.
Guest reports missing confirmation, incorrect reservation details, pending status or property unable to locate a booking.

• Acknowledge the issue and collect reservation ID if available.
• Complete approved guest verification before disclosing reservation information.
• Open the authoritative reservation record and confirm status, property, dates and room details.
• Compare the record with the guest's confirmation and classify the issue: pending, confirmed, discrepancy, not found or property mismatch.
• For a confirmed booking, contact the property through the approved channel if property-side confirmation is needed.
• For corrections or changes, follow POL-GST-002 and the authorised transaction workflow.
• Record evidence references, actions, owner and next step; escalate unresolved discrepancies.

Do not call a pending request confirmed. Do not promise a modification, cancellation or refund under this SOP. If no record is found, do not advise the guest to book again until duplicate/payment risk has been checked.
Close only when status is verified, the guest has received an accurate update and any required follow-up owner is assigned.
Guest asks to cancel a reservation or disputes a cancellation outcome.

• Verify the guest and reservation ID.
• Retrieve the reservation-specific cancellation terms accepted at checkout.
• Check request timestamp against the recorded deadline and conditions.
• Explain eligibility and any fee only when supported by the reservation record.
• Submit cancellation only through an authorised workflow and with required guest confirmation.
• Verify the reservation status changed and record the cancellation reference.
• If refund is queried, follow SOP-003; do not promise a refund amount or timing.
Escalate unclear terms, partner-initiated cancellation, system failure, suspected misleading checkout display or exception requests.
Cancellation status and guest communication are recorded; any refund follow-up is separately tracked.
Guest asks whether a refund is due, initiated, delayed or completed.

• Verify guest and reservation.
• Locate the related payment transaction and cancellation/refund decision.
• Determine whether the request is eligible, under review, initiated, processing or completed.
• Use the payment/provider record as evidence; do not rely only on an internal note.
• Communicate the exact recorded status and any sourced estimate with a no-guarantee qualification.
• Escalate missing references, failed refund instructions or timeline beyond the recorded estimate.
• Log transaction reference, status, date checked and next action.
Do not label a refund complete before provider confirmation. Do not invent processing timelines or deductions.
Guest receives an evidence-based status and unresolved financial action has an assigned owner.
Guest reports failed payment, amount debited without confirmation, repeated charge or duplicate transaction.

• Verify guest and reservation context without collecting card secrets or OTPs.
• Collect transaction reference, amount, currency and approximate timestamp; mask sensitive details.
• Check reservation status and payment ledger/provider status.
• Classify as failed, authorised/pending, captured, duplicate captured or unresolved.
• For pending/failed transactions, explain only the provider status and approved next step.
• For duplicate captured transactions or mismatch, raise a finance/payment case with transaction references.
• Check reservation creation separately; do not infer confirmation from a debit alert.
• Record case ID and follow-up owner.
Never ask for full card number, CVV, password, PIN or OTP. Escalate suspected fraud immediately.
Payment status is verified or escalated with a traceable case and owner.
Guest reports inability to check in, room not ready, reservation not recognised or access instruction failure.

• Verify guest and confirmed reservation; confirm stay dates and property.
• Check property-specific check-in time and arrival instructions in the reservation/listing.
• Ask for the property response and relevant reference without requesting unnecessary personal data.
• Contact the property through the approved partner channel and confirm reservation mapping and room readiness.
• For denied access or unresolved confirmed booking, escalate to the duty/incident route.
• Communicate verified facts and realistic next steps; record all contact attempts.
If the guest reports immediate danger, medical emergency or threat, prioritise local emergency assistance and the urgent incident procedure.
Access is resolved or an authorised escalation owner has accepted the case.
Guest reports cleanliness, room condition, missing amenity or material mismatch with listing.

• Acknowledge the concern and determine whether there is an immediate safety issue.
• Verify reservation and property; capture room/issue details and time observed.
• Request relevant evidence only through approved secure channels; avoid unnecessary sensitive images.
• Compare the complaint with listing details and property response.
• Offer only remedies authorised in the resolution matrix; do not promise compensation or refund.
• Escalate health/safety, severe cleanliness, misrepresentation or repeated unresolved issues.
• Record guest impact, evidence reference, property response and action owner.
Guest receives an approved resolution or a named escalation owner and next update expectation.
Partner contacts support about onboarding, listing, reservations, account access or settlement.

• Verify partner account and requester authority using the approved partner process.
• Classify the request: onboarding, listing content, reservation, cancellation, account or settlement.
• Retrieve the relevant partner record and applicable policy.
• Explain requirements using current recorded information; do not invent commercial terms or deadlines.
• For account, ownership or payout changes, use enhanced verification and authorised workflow.
• Route financial, content-compliance or technical issues to the designated owner.
• Record partner ID, request, evidence references, action and next step.
Never request partner passwords, OTPs or full banking credentials. Treat bank-detail changes as high risk.
Request is completed in the authoritative partner system or accepted by an accountable specialist.
Issue exceeds agent authority, has unresolved conflicting evidence, presents safety/security risk or has significant guest/partner impact.

• Urgent: immediate safety threat, suspected account/payment compromise, serious privacy exposure or guest stranded without safe accommodation.
• High: confirmed reservation not honoured, significant financial discrepancy, repeated property failure or material service disruption.
• Standard: unresolved policy interpretation, routine listing correction or non-urgent account issue.

• Stabilise the interaction and prioritise immediate safety/security steps.
• Capture affected reservation/partner ID, timestamps, concise facts and evidence references.
• Do not collect secrets or speculate about root cause.
• Select the appropriate incident category and severity using the approved support system.
• Route to the designated team/queue and obtain acknowledgement where required.
• Tell the guest/partner what is known, what happens next and when an update is expected only if a verified service target exists.
• Maintain an audit trail of decisions, handoffs and updates.
The accountable owner confirms resolution or formally accepts ongoing ownership; incident records contain outcome and learnings.
